offence_severity: Rigorous imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs.10,000/- each
physical_harm: Firearm entry wounds, exit wounds, and injuries caused by axes and pitchforks
number_of_offences: Six offences/counts charged, three finally upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The statements of the eye-witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) were almost identical and there were no major contradictions between them. The medical evidence fully corroborated the prosecution story, including the injuries caused by firearms and sharp-edged weapons.
witness_credibility: The court assessed that the witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) were credible as their statements were almost identical, corroborated by PW-4 and medical evidence, and supported the prosecution's version of events despite minor variations and contradictions.
trial_duration: Trial court acquitted all the accused; High Court set aside the judgment of the Trial Court and found A-2, A-4 and A-5 guilty; Supreme Court dismissed the appeal
legal_representation: Rajiv Dutta, Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Advs., Dr. Rajeev Sharma, Bhanwarpal Singh Jadon, Umesh Gupta, Raghuvir Sharma, Advs. for the Appellants; Ms. Sansriti Pathak, Krishnanand Pandeya, Advs. for the Respondent
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court acquitted all the accused; High Court set aside the judgment of the Trial Court and found A-2, A-4 and A-5 guilty; Supreme Court dismissed the appeal
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that six persons, including two with guns, killed the victim in broad daylight. The statements of the eye-witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) were corroborated by PW-4 and medical evidence, supporting the prosecution's version of events.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the statements of the eye-witnesses (PW-1 and PW-2) should not be relied upon due to their close relationship with the deceased and enmity between the parties. They also questioned the credibility of the FIR and the medical evidence.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the presence of eye-witnesses and their statements, when corroborated by other evidence, can be relied upon to establish the facts of the case.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the Court found the prosecution's version of the events, supported by the eye-witnesses and medical evidence, credible and that the accused were guilty of the offences punishable under Sections 147, 148, 302/149 of the IPC.
other_sentence_order: The accused were sentenced to rigorous imprisonment for life and a fine of Rs.10,000/- each for the offence under Section 302 read with 149, IPC.
